title: Mechanical Chest Compression Device (Corpuls cpr®)
content_markdown:
#### Indications

- Patients indicated for intra-arrest transport 
- Chest compression quality is poor due to rescuer fatigue
- Scene environmental factors make the provision of quality chest compression difficult or cause protracted chest compression pause times associated with rescuer rotation 

#### Contraindications

- Chest height < 14cm or > 34cm, refer to chest height gauge 
- Unable to position safely and correctly on the thorax 
- Patients with injuries that lead to an instability of the thorax and thus prevent effective mechanical CPR (mCPR)- Traumatic arrest
Refer to cardiac arrest guidelines for the contraindications of intra-arrest transportation 

#### Complications

- Procedural delays of chest compressions or defibrillation during application
- Suboptimal compressions due to misalignment or incorrect configuration
- Iatrogenic injuries (e.g. rib fractures, dermal abrasions, solid organ trauma, or foetal injury)
Due to misplacement or migration. Constantly reassess stamp position to ensure patient safety.

#### Pre-shift Check

- Check all equipment is in the bag
- Check Corpuls cpr\xae equipment is clean and not damaged
- Ensure securing straps are fastened to Recboard, and the straps to secure for extrication are clipped into their fasteners- Ensure sufficient battery charge and rotate batteries every shift- Check both stamps for wear and cracks- Ensure short stamp is inserted into Corpuls cpr\xae piston as default- Turn device on and check for alarms or errors and passes self-test. Turn device off once completed.
#### Equipment Required

##### Essentials

- Corpuls: 
- Corpuls cpr\xae Arm
- Stamps
- Recboard- Fixation Ring- Chest height gauge- Pen (where possible, skin marker type)- Extrication aid (e.g. CombiCarrier)
#### Procedure

#### 1. Preparation Checklist

- Confirm patient meets indications for a MCCD
- Use the chest height gauge to determine patient suitability and stamp size- Ensure adequate space and people for application- If resources permit, assign roles to simultaneously prepare for extrication - Where possible, have an advanced airway placed prior to application- Ensure IV/IO are firmly secured- Ensure patient’s chest and back are free of clothing- Remove any impediments (e.g. compression puck, jewellery, ECG leads, etc)- Maintain uninterrupted manual compressions during device assembly
#### 2. Corpuls Assembly 

- Securely insert the Corpuls cpr\xae Arm into the Recboard’s socket
Ensure its balanced and will not tip over

- Select appropriate stamp size for chest height and insert: 
- Short stamp: Chest height of 20 cm – 34 cm
- Tall stamp (paeds/small adults): Chest height of 14 cm – 27 cm
- **DO NOT** use Corpuls without stamp. This may result in serious injury

- Turn on Corpuls and ensures it passes self-test

- Confirm compression settings 
- Compression Ratio: 
- Continuous (default), or 
- 30:2 or 15:2 based on clinical context

- Asynchronous Ventilation Rate 
- 10 bpm (default)
- To change rate: Settings → Ventilation → cont. → Rate [1/min] → +/- to desired rate → tick symbol to confirm- Depth: 
- 5cm (default), or
- adjust to 1/3 of patient’s chest depth when required (max 6cm)- Rate: 
- 110 compressions per minute (default)

#### 3. Application

- Orientate the Corpuls cpr\xae so the CPR Arm will be located at the left shoulder of the patient

- STAGE ONE: 

- Airway Paramedic: slightly lift the patient’s head ≈5cm,

- Corpuls ICP: slide the Corpuls recboard under the head so it is flush with the patient’s shoulders.

- STAGE TWO: 

- Ensure COACHED/defibrillation is not impacted.

- Confirm roles, explain process and emphasise minimising interruptions to compressions. 
- Airway Paramedic: Lift and protects head, secures airway adjunct.
- Compression Performer: Assists with elevating one side of torso
- a	Additional Resource/s: Assists with elevating opposite side of torso, dry a diaphoretic patient’s back
- ICP: While holding onto Corpuls Arm, slides recboard under the thorax. 

- Pause compressions, safely elevate the patient’s torso 5- 15cm and slide recboard under patient. 

- Immediately re-commence manual compressions.
Stage Two, iii-iv, must not exceed 5 seconds in duration.

- STAGE THREE: 

- With locking lever open, manoeuvre Corpuls Arm over patient as close to sternum as possible without impacting manual compression.

- Pause compressions and align Corpuls Arm so stamp is over the **middle** of the patient’s sternum (compression zone). 

- Lower and manoeuvre Corpulse Arm onto the sternum until the Start/Stop LED Button illuminates green.

- **With an open palm**, close locking lever

- Press the Start/Stop LED Button to begin mechanical compressions. 
Stage Three, ii-v, must not exceed 5 seconds in duration.
The compression will increase to the full depth by the 4th compression 
Depth will be restricted if the Corpuls cpr\xae determines the set depth requires excessive force

- Using a skin maker pen, trace around the stamp. This action provides a quick reference to determine if the stamp has become mal positioned 

- To prevent injury to the patient, continually monitor that the stamp is in the correct location, ESPECIALLY after moving the patient. Immediately reposition if necessary 

#### 4. During cardiac arrest

- IPPV may be delivered in synch with when Start/Stop LED Button flashes blue.
Remember to consider individual patient needs when choosing ventilations rates (10 ventilations per minute for adult, 15 ventilations for < 12 years of age).

- To ‘evaluate rhythm’ during a COACHED cycle, the Corpuls cpr\xae compressions will need to be paused at “hands off” step
Ideally the person assigned to press the “shock” button will also be responsible for pausing and restarting the Corpuls cpr\xae compressions during COACHED 

#### 5. Securing the Fixation Ring

- With the silver button facing up, and with mechanical compressions ongoing, slide Fixation Ring under stamp until the stamp is operating at the centre of the ring. 

- Until secured, ensure a person hold the Fixation Ring in place.

- Use the magnetic clasps to attach Recboard straps to the Fixation Ring 

- To ensure Fixation Ring remains central, coordinate tightening of diagonally opposite Recboard straps.
Straps should be a firm fit but not so much as to impeded ventilations and chest recoil.

#### 6. Extrication

**Principles:**

- If resources permit, simultaneously plan and prepare for extrication during Corpuls cpr\xae application
- Extrication methods will depend on the context of the location and environment. The Corpuls cpr\xae can be used with either the CombiCarrier or carry sheet technique- Notify receiving hospital as soon as practical- The stretcher must be flat as possible to reduce risk of Corpuls migrating. Remove any items that impede the stretcher to being flat- Reboard straps must be maximally tightened prior to preparing for extrication. Remember to loosen to minimal acceptable tightness once extrication is completed- Throughout care and after moving, the stamp and Fixation Ring location can migrate. Continually monitor that the stamp and ring are in the correct position. When needed, adjust straps to ensure they are still firm or cease device, begin manual compressions, then readjust location before recommencing mechanical compressions- Throughout extrication preparation and process, continue with mechanical compressions, ventilations, COACHED and necessary drug administrations- If needing to move the patient horizontally, do not drag the patient by the Corpuls cpr\xae. This can cause misalignment and potential injuries to the patient - Balance the patient’s presenting condition (e.g. sustained non-shockable rhythm) and complexity of extrication when considering the delay of COAHCED
- CombiCarrier (Option 1): 

- Place the CombiCarrier at the base of feet

- Split the CombiCarrier at the head end with the feet end still together 

- While elevating the patient’s legs, slide the split CombiCarrier along each side of the patient 

- Using the extrication/transport straps attached to the Recboard, lift one side of the patient’s torso and slide the first half of the CombCarrier under the patient. 

- Repeat on the other side and slide the other half of the CombiCarrier under the patient while connecting the head end of the CombiCarrier together 

- Confirm Corpuls is still operating within the compression zone. Adjust if required.

- Secure Recboard to CombiCarrier with Corpuls extrication/transport straps and secure the patient’s hands/waist and legs to the CombiCarrier with the approved CombiCarrier straps

- Lift and extricate as per standard manual handling practices

- CombiCarrier (Option 2): 

- Split the CombiCarrier both ends and align each side next to patient

- Starting at the feet end, elevate the patient’s legs, slide the first half of the CombiCarrier under legs. Repeat process for the other half, and secure the feet end of the CombiCarrier together 

- Using the extrication/transport straps attached to the Recboard, lift one side of the patient’s torso and slide the first half of the CombiCarrier under the patient. 

- Repeat on the other side and slide the other half of the CombiCarrier under the patient while connecting the head end of the CombiCarrier together 

- Confirm Corpuls is still operating within the compression zone. Adjust if required.

- Secure Recboard to CombiCarrier with Corpuls extrication/transport straps and secure the patient’s hands/waist and legs to the CombiCarrier with the approved CombiCarrier straps

- Lift and extricate as per standard manual handling practices

- Carry sheet: 

- Use as per standard manual handling practices

- Perform minimal log roll and place carry sheet halfway under the patient.

- Repeat minimal log roll on other side and unfurl carry sheet.

- Confirm Corpuls is still operating within the compression zone. Adjust if required.

- Lift and extricate as per standard manual handling practices.

#### 7. Cardiac arrest during transportation with no Corpuls cpr\xae yet to be in situ

- Stop the ambulance in a safe place. 

- Prioritise high quality CPR and COACHED.

- If safe, move patient on the stretcher out to the back of the ambulance.
The ambulance may need to be relocated to avoid hazards such as traffic.

- Continue with ALS, then apply and secure Corpuls cpr\xae as per section 3.
The stretcher will need to be lowered to facilitate safe lifting mechanics. 

- Load patient and resume transport and care as required. 

#### 8. Transportation

##### Principles

- Continue with mechanical compressions and ALS. 
- Seat belts may cross the compression zone, but they do not impede quality of compressions. However, the seatbelts might obscure the compression zone, so extra vigilance is required to ensure the stamp has not migrated. - Develop a plan to manage potential ROSC during extrication and/or transport.

- If the CombiCarrier was used to extricate, this must first be removed prior to seatbelt application.

- Apply stretcher seatbelts across patient in usual manner.

#### 9. Hospital Handover

##### Principles

- ACTAS to continue ALS until handover is complete and patient is transferred to hospital bed.
- Provide a ‘hands-off handover’ prior to transferring patient hospital bed- ACTAS Corpuls to remain on patient (including ROSC patients) 
#### Alarm Troubleshooting

#### System error / malfunction

- **Consequence:** Therapy failure
- **Action:**
- Perform manual compressions. 
- Restart Corpuls. If alarm persists inform DOO and replace unit.

#### Battery low / Temperature high / Not ready for use

- **Consequence:** Therapy failure
- **Action:**
- Perform manual compressions
- Replace battery
- Consider plugging into external power source if available.
#### Therapy stopped for longer than 8 seconds

- **Consequence:** Therapy failure
- **Action:**
- If compressions no longer required – cancel alarm
- If compressions still required: 
- Restart therapy using Start/Stop Button
- Cancel the alarm
- If alarm persists and unable to restart device, perform manual compressions.
#### Locking lever has not been opened or closed

- **Consequence:** Therapy failure
- **Action:**
- Open/close the locking lever

#### Arm set too low

- **Consequence:** Inadequate therapy
- **Action:**
- Adjust Arm position up.

#### Arm temperature too high

- **Consequence:** Imminent Arm failure and inadequate therapy
- **Action:**
- Perform manual compressions

#### Specified depth not achieved

- **Consequence:** Thorax is rigid, and specified depth is not achieved
- **Action:**
- Assess quality of compressions, consider manual CPR if determined to be ineffective.

#### Specific Notes

##### Considerations

- For critically ill patients, not in cardiac arrest, but have a high likelihood of arresting, consider applying and securing Corpuls cpr\xae to these patients (e.g. ROSC) prior to extrication and or transportation
- If ROSC is achieved while device is in situ, pause the device. The stamp alignment can be left hovering over the compression zone to minimize hands-off time if patient re-arrests - To ensure adequate positioning for advanced airway insertion (e.g. sniffing position), the arm height may need to be adjusted and straps for the Fixation Ring will need to be loosened or removed- To prevent skill decay, it is advised that clinicians, at minimum, should refresh their Corpuls cpr\xae knowledge and skills every 3 months. Suggested learning exercises include simulation, skill stations, and the eLearn package/s
